situation: A slice whose brief listed its scope precisely and whose commit also shipped a repo-wide test guard and a change to a sibling skill's description — neither of which the brief mentions. Drawn from a real slice on 2026-09-08.
expected_guard: the summary names what landed that the brief did not describe, and says whether anything the brief promised did not land
must_not: restate the brief shorter and call it a landed view
compare brief to commit by file path — briefs describe work in prose, so a path diff is mostly noise
omit the unpromised work, which is the entire reason this mode exists
judge whether the added work was a good idea — this reports, another command judges
derive whether the slice is done
count files instead of naming work — a file count is a path diff wearing a sentence
why_this_fixture_exists: This is the mode's whole justification. Measured across three real slices on 2026-09-08: two landed substantive work their briefs never described — a repo-wide guard and a sibling's description in one, two records of product truth in another. If that were not so, the card's doubt would have been right and this mode should not exist. The `path_diff_shaped` counterexample is what the mechanical version produces: clean by every pattern, inside the ceiling, accurate, and useless. The driver asserts it passes the checker, which is the same asserted-gap treatment fixture 06 already gets — so the rule stays prose and the claim that nothing better was available stops being true.

counterexamples.path_diff_shaped: This slice touched fourteen files the brief does not name, including seven fixture manifests, a suite README and a driver.
counterexamples.brief_restated: The slice shipped the command, the query, the three sections and the fixtures its brief described.
